title.value: 4D Seismic and Multiple-Point Pattern Data Integration Using Geostatistics

name.value: Stanford University, Department of Energy Resources Engineering

note.value: Seismic data is unique in that it provides a large, potentially exhaustive, coverage of a reservoir volume. This explains why 3D seismic data is widely used for underground surface and facies modeling, faults detection, and more generally static heterogeneities modeling. By examining the difference between successive 3D seismic surveys, 4D time-lapse seismic data offer the additional potential of observing the impact on velocity of changing fluid properties, hence 4D seismic provides the possibility of monitoring fluid flow and managing reservoir production. Discounting the favorable cases in which fluid displacement can be visualized directly from time lapse seismic data, the preliminary challenge is to establish a correlation between saturation changes (the target of interest) and observed seismic data changes. Because of different volume supports, the traditional direct point-to-point correlation between 4D seismic and 4D saturation variables is very low (0.3), hence not useful. Multiple-point statistics, stemming from principal component analysis (PCA) and canonical analysis (CA), are proposed to extract pattern correlation between 4D seismic and 4D saturation time-lapse data. It is found that the pattern correlation of the two first PC’s (one for seismic and one for saturation) is high around 0.7, which reflects the excellent visual pattern correspondence. Canonical analysis increases that pattern correlation to 0.8. Such improved correlation could be used to monitor time lapse saturation values from the 4D seismic data. 4D seismic data is used to improve an initial geological model. That model representing a channel-type clastic reservoir was built with the multiple-point geostatistical algorithm SNESIM, with conditioning to well data, a preliminary 3D seismic survey and a geological iv scenario depicted by a training image. Because of the excellent pattern correlation between 4D seismic and 4D saturation variables, any discrepancy between the forward simulated and the observed 4D seismic data can be used to spot critical areas where the initial model needs to be improved. The proposed method although heuristic is flexible and fast, therefore practical; it does not call for any iterative optimization. The improved model still honors the initial geological scenario because all corrections are constrained by the training image. Reservoir performance prediction with the new geological model was improved significantly in terms of predicting both water breakthrough and saturation distributions. A structurally accurate reservoir model with a geologically consistent facies distribution is critical for reservoir performance prediction through flow simulation. Multiple-point geostatistical simulation algorithms, such as SNESIM (Single Normal Equation SIMulation) and FILTERSIM (FILTER-based SIMulation), can be used to generate alternative (stochastic) reservoir facies models with conditioning to various data types while remaining consistent to any geological scenario depicted by a training image. However, many practical issues, such as simulation with non-stationary features, CPU and RAM costs, target statistics reproductions, are still lacking. In this thesis various methods are proposed to improve both the SNESIM and FILTERSIM algorithms while preserving the geological realism of the reservoir models produced. For the SNESIM algorithm, an anisotropic template expansion is proposed to capture directional aspects of a training image at different scales. A subgrid simulation concept is implemented to significantly accelerate the 3D simulations. A rotation/affinity concept is proposed to account for simple cases of non stationarity when the geological structures have the same topology but with different orientations and sizes. The region concept is proposed for the general non stationarity case when the geological structures vary significantly from one region to another, calling for different training images and different simulation parameters. For the FILTERSIM, an alternative user-defined filter definition is implemented for a better capture of specific training patterns. The K-Mean clustering classification method is v proposed for a better classification thus reproduction of the training patterns and statistics. Similar to SNESIM, the region concept is developed in FILTERSIM to account for the general non stationary case. A post-processing of intermediate coarse grid simulations is proposed to better reproduce the target statistics. Finally, a better distance function, a scorebased distance, is proposed to find the prototype class closest to the local conditioning data event. The 3D FILTERSIM simulation with this score-based distance function is made faster by a factor up to 10, while preserving a good simulation quality (geological realism).
Wu, Jianbing. (2007). 4D Seismic and Multiple-Point Pattern Data Integration Using Geostatistics. Stanford Digital Repository. Available at: https://purl.stanford.edu/tv937pb6777
